key_insight: A newly built image dataset showed that transfer learning, especially VGG16, can classify topological relationships between objects more accurately than traditional machine learning models.
clinical_relevance: In medical imaging, this kind of spatial relationship recognition could help support tasks like anatomy interpretation, lesion localization, and segmentation quality checks.
method: Built a labeled dataset of 11,000+ images covering key topological relationships
Extracted features using segmentation, contour detection, and grayscale normalization
Compared classic models (Naive Bayes, KNN, Random Forest, SVM, ANN) with deep models (VGG16, InceptionResNetV2)
evidence_signal: VGG16 achieved the strongest performance, with validation accuracy reaching 89.55%, outperforming the traditional models on the new dataset.
watch_item: Results come from a newly created dataset, so generalization to other medical imaging settings and real-world clinical images still needs careful validation.
paper_title: Exploring Learning Models for Topological Relationship Recognition from Image Data
